cases.name: Emily Andrea Traynor
cases.about:
She was a home healthcare provider.

Her obituary said, "Emily was born in Hannibal and grew up in Bowling Green before later making her home in Hannibal.
She was surrounded by family and friends who loved her deeply. Emily had a tender soul and a curious, creative heart. She loved nature - especially butterflies - and could spend hours taking pictures of the sky or anything that caught her eye outdoors. She loved animals, painting, reading, traveling, good food, and curling up for a cozy nap whenever the world felt too loud. More than anything, she adored her two younger brothers, Kole and Darin, who brought endless laughter and light to her days.

Much like the butterflies she loved, Emily’s words remind us to live freely and with grace: “Don’t spend your whole life wishing it away. Get out and do it.” “Mistakes are a part of being human. Appreciate your mistakes for what they are… precious life lessons that can only be learned the hard way. Don’t forget to smile today.”
cases.narrative: Detective Jordan Freiling testified about the wounds to the Traynor. The autopsy revealed 33 knife wounds in all. Traynor was cut or stabbed in the hip, the chest, the neck, the back and the side of her face and head. “Two kitchen knives were found on the floor with what appeared to blood,” Freiling said.
